title: Bought a rental in 2026? Ready to rent decides it

beats.text: Depreciation starts when it's *ready and available* to rent.

captions.instagram:
Bought a rental in 2026? The date it's ready to rent decides when depreciation starts, not the closing date.

✔️ The IRS says you place a rental in service when it's ready and available for rent. A tenant doesn't have to have moved in.
✔️ Listed and ready by Dec 31: depreciation can start on your 2026 return.
✔️ Still under renovation on Dec 31: it starts in 2027.
✔️ Land is never depreciated, so split the price between land and building.
✔️ A residential rental building is depreciated over 27.5 years.

Keep the listing date and photos as proof.
Send this to a friend who just bought a rental.

Source: IRS Publication 527. General information, not advice for your situation.
captions.youtube_title: Bought a Rental in 2026? When Depreciation Starts (Placed in Service)
captions.youtube_description: Rental property is placed in service when it's ready and available for rent, even if no tenant has moved in. Ready by December 31 means depreciation can start for 2026; still under renovation means it starts later. Land can't be depreciated, so allocate the purchase price between land and building. Residential rental property is depreciated over 27.5 years under GDS. Source: IRS Publication 527.
